In May of 1990, the Citizens Committee for the Homeless, a Santa Cruz County nonprofit organization, began a new project by opening the gates of an organic garden on Pelton Avenue. The Homeless Garden Project would provide job training and meaningful work in a therapeutic environment. The Homeless Garden Project began as a place to provide sanctuary, refuge, and meaningful work within the healing space of the organic farm. Blossoming over time and furthering the project's benefits, the farm harvests have provided an opportunity to support our vision and community through our CSA program, farm stand, and crafts, which are sold at our local Santa Cruz stores & online. We are genuinely humbled by the profound transformations our trainees make in our job training program, and the generous support

listings.name: Two Roots Farm
listings.address: 100 Sopris Creek Rd, Basalt, CO, USA
listings.description: Two Roots Farm has been growing vegetables, herbs, and flowers for the Roaring Fork Valley using regenerative methods since 2016. We aim to grow food in the cleanest, healthiest way possible: prioritizing the vitality of our farmers, soil, and eaters above all else. We use organic growing practices, minimum tillage, biodynamic compost, crop rotations, increased biodiversity, and sustainable methods to grow the best produce possible without the use of any chemicals, herbicides, or pesticides. We rely on integrated pest management, building healthy soil, and hard working farmers to maintain a vibrant farm. Our pastures are managed using management-intensive rotational grazing, no-spray, and no-till methods. We sell our produce into the Roaring Fork Valley through a CSA, an onsite farm stand, and local restaurants. Two Roots Farm provides produce to Lift Up (Basalt- Rifle grassroots food insecurity organization), the Pitkin County Senior Center, and regional food pantries.

listings.name: Kai-Kai Farm
listings.address: 8006 Southwest Kanner Highway, Indiantown, FL, USA
listings.description: Kai-Kai Farm promotes just and equitable food for our local communities by conserving natural resources, providing economic prices, and improve health outcomes. We have a unique variety of hospitality sites to choose from that support several operations such as our farm market, CSA, and farm to table dinners. Kai-Kai Farm is the first to operate an established farm market and CSA program in Indiantown, offering fresh produce to its neighbors. Our direct sale approach permits high quality communication and relationships between farmer and consumer. We are very fortunate to have cultivated close relationships with some of the best local chefs and restaurants in Palm Beach and Martin County. Kai-Kai Farm picturesque landscapes capture everyone\'s vision and turns them into unforgettable memories. Our towering eucalyptus trees, flower fields, horizon views, and vegetables make for a selection of whimsical surroundings for all events and photoshoots.
listings.locationNote: Directions to the Kai-Kai Farm: From the South, take I-95 North, Exit 96 for Hobe Sound, head West on Bridge Rd. Continue past Pratt Whitney, then turn left at Kanner Hwy (76) junction. Go west 3.5 miles on Kanner Hwy toward Indiantown. From the North, head South on I-95, Exit 101 onto FL-76 (Kanner Hwy) and head SW toward Indiantown. Go 7.5 miles then look for Kai-Kai Farm on the left.
production: Fair labor practices, living wage, fair trade, etc.
organizations: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services and Florida Agritourism Association
listings.seasonNote: Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) is about a direct relationship between farmer and consumer. Rather than simply purchasing food, our customers buy shares of the farm's harvest in advance so we can pay for seeds, equipment and labor. A "share" is a number of prepaid and prescheduled boxes of hand picked produce from our farm. The farmers choose what goes in the box and shareholders choose how many boxes and when they'd like to pick up each box. Each CSA box is full of an average of 10-12 retail portions of freshly harvested vegetables and greens (including tomatoes in season) all grown at Kai-Kai Farm. Unwanted items may be swapped (but not credited) for other retail produce on hand. We're not here to simply sell you a product – we're interested in opening our fields to you, getting to know you, and helping you get to know your food. As the saying goes “Know your farmer, know your food.”

listings.name: Waianae Farmers Market
listings.description: Waiʻanae moku once known for the abundance of food produced from their rich vertisol soils. Now faces some of the highest rates of health inequalities related to food. With the lowest average household income many community members does not have the purchasing power to access healthy affordable food, therefore they either skip a meal or purchase cheap high calorie low nutrient foods. Leading to numerous health challenges that includes high rates of obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases/conditions, and cancer. Mākeke Waiʻanae is a farmers market that perpetuates a social, economic and intellectual space for community members, and vendors to access an equitable and sustainable farmers market.

listings.description: Instead of just focusing on family staples, Firefly Gardens also includes rare heirloom varieties that you may not have heard of or otherwise not have the opportunity to try. Some of these Varieties include the art of taste datil, lemon basil, heirloom tomatoes, and much more. We have add on products such as, our bread and bakery shares, Coffee from our roastery, tea, eggs, honey and medicinal herbs. Currently We are not certified Organic, but we do follow all Organic practices. We do not use any herbicide or pesticides. We focus on creating habitats for natural predators and natural mulching techniques. Our gardens are fertilized only with our onsite compost which is comprised of organic material, leaves and clippings from our garden and food scraps from our homestead.

listings.name: New Roots for Refugees Farm Share
listings.address: 100 Richmond Avenue, Kansas City, KS, USA
listings.description: New Roots for Refugees Farm Share is a CSA (Community Supported Agriculture) program that provides subscribers with 5-7 locally-grown, seasonal vegetables and herbs each week (AKA a “share”). Shares can be picked up at one of our pick-up sites around the greater Kansas City area. New Roots aggregates produce from farmers currently in our 4-year program, as well as graduates from the program. Payment is made in advance or in installments and helps provide capital for things such as seeds and tools for farmers to use in preparation for the growing season. Our farmers are experienced growers who are learning to farm in a new climate while also learning a new language and food culture. By buying a Farm Share, you are supporting the training and establishment of multiple farmers in the Kansas City area and directly helping grow the number of urban farmers!
listings.locationNote: New Roots for Refugees farmers grow produce at Juniper Gardens Training Farm located at 100 Richmond Ave. Kansas City, KS 66101. We are offer Farm Share pick-up locations at various sites around the greater Kansas City area.
organizations: Catholic Charities of NE Kansas, Cultivate KC

listings.description: We are currently growing on two plots of land located just southeast of Hillsboro North Dakota. Our home plot is a third of an acre, this is where we started our farming adventure back in 2020. The new farm plot is ten acres located a few miles north of our home plot, we started growing here in 2023. On both of our farm plots we intercrop our annual vegetables with our perennial fruits in hope of increasing our production in small spaces. We are currently growing everything that can survive in our climate in the hopes of bringing a diverse array of crops that aren’t common in our local markets.

We will send out a weekly email with our harvest list so you can get an idea of what will be delivered to you that week.

Good Rain Farm is primarily an Indigenous Femme led and operated mixed produce Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) farm with an emphasis on Indigenous First Foods. We also raise heritage breed Champagne d’Argent meat rabbits to provide full dietary and meal options to our members, a nod to Farmer Michelle's family heritage. The principles of Good Rain Farm are decolonizing diets, revitalizing culture, food sovereignty and the returning to reverent sustainable land stewardship. Currently x̌ast sq̓it serves over 150 families in the greater Portland Metro area, with 50% of its produce going free to the end-user.

listings.name: Weavers Way Farm Market
listings.description: We grow food for and with the community on our two farm sites in Northwest Philly while also providing farm jobs in the city for new and beginning farmers. We also offer experiential, outdoor learning opportunities for Saul High School students. By buying a share in the CSA, you are supporting a unique model of participatory community agriculture, jobs for new and beginning farmers, and on-farm education for Saul students and everyone else who participates in our farms. During the season, shareholders come to the farm once a week to collect their share of that week’s harvest. We offer pickup times at the farm three times a week — Tuesdays and Fridays from 2-7 p.m. and Saturdays from 10 a.m. -4 p.m. Shares come in two sizes. Shares come in two sizes: small share consists of 5-6 units of vegetables and is recommended for two people. A large share consists is twice as big and is recommended for four people. We have Summer and Fall CSA programs.
listings.locationNote: Parking options: Upon entering the parking next to the Farm Market (watch for Farm Market signs), you can park at the first parking lot to the right, or in the grass in front of the pasture to the left of the livestock barn. There is also street parking on Henry Ave. or Cinnaminson Street (then use the crosswalk to cross Henry Ave.)

listings.description: Hillside Haven Farm offers a wide variety of fresh, naturally grown produce. Conveniently located close to Elizabethton & Johnson City TN, Banner Elk & Boone NC. Enjoy local and healthy vegetables through easy online ordering, local farmers markets, and weekly CSA memberships! Farm pickup and local meet-up or drop-off points are also available. Healthy food comes from healthy roots! Soil health at Hillside Haven Farm is built and maintained naturally through organic material composting practices, rotational and companion planting, and soil testing. No chemical fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, or additives are used at any point during production. Customers also appreciate access to farm-fresh flavors from Hillside Haven Farm outside of regular farmers market season, thanks to the use of high tunnels to extend the growing season.

listings.name: Athens, Tx Farmers Market
listings.address: 110 West Tyler Street, Athens, TX, USA
listings.description: The Athens, TX Farmers Market, held every Saturday from 9a to 1p (closing at 12 p.m. during the summer) at 110 W. Tyler St. in historic downtown Athens, is a vibrant, community-rooted marketplace showcasing the best of East Texas. Established in 2012, the market features local farmers, ranchers, bakers, and artisans who offer fresh produce, pasture-raised meats, handmade foods, and unique goods—all grown or made within the region. With a strong focus on seasonal quality and local sourcing, the market invites visitors to shop with purpose, connect with producers, and experience the charm and flavor of Athens firsthand. Established in 2012 and stewarded by local organizer DJ Warren, this local sourced market brings together more than 50 vendors offering locally grown produce, pasture-raised meats, fresh-baked goods, artisan crafts, flowers, and hand‑made foods—all sourced directly from small family farms and local artisans. It’s our commitment to our community, 14 years strong!
listings.locationNote: In the heart of downtown Athens— west side of the square.

listings.name: Lynchburg Grows Veggie Box CSA
listings.description: Lynchburg Grows is a nonprofit urban farm. Our mission is to work with our community to provide access to healthy food and afford purposeful jobs to individuals with disabilities. We have a 200-member CSA program and an on-site Farm Store open every Thursday, 9am to 1pm, throughout the growing season. Whether customers shop at the Farm Store or join the CSA, they can get the produce we raise, using all organic methods, plus produce and fruit from other local farms, local eggs, and artisanal foods. A scholarship fund makes CSA memberships available to people who need financial help to join. SNAP/EBT users get 50% off their CSA memberships and Farm Store purchases of fruit and vegetables. We also run a produce prescription program in partnership with Virginia Cooperative Extension, called FreshRx, which provides nutrition and cooking education along with free produce and we donate produce to area organizations working to help meet basic needs in the community.

listings.name: Chewelah Farmers Market
listings.address: 700 N Park St, Chewelah, WA, USA
listings.description: The Chewelah Farmers Market is a non-profit and is run entirely by volunteers. The market is known for its vendor-friendly policies. Many of our vendors will tell you that this is their favorite market! And our monthly special event days have garnered a following all of their own. Where else can you race a zucchini down the creek or shoot cherries at a target with a slingshot? The Chewelah Farmers Market was selected by the Washington State Farmers' Market Association as the Best Small Farmers' Market in the state for 2010 and 2011. The mission is to make available high-quality, locally produced food and to promote self-sufficiency in the community food systems by providing a venue for local farmers, growers and producers to connect directly with consumers and to support educational opportunities. We invite you to come on down to the beautiful Chewelah City Park on Fridays, mid-May through mid-October, and enjoy all that the Chewelah Farmers Market has to offer.
listings.locationNote: NW corner of the Chewelah City Park on Highway 395
